subject: Regional reserved capacity pricing, discounts & DR/replication options
messages:
From: Adam Lowe <adam.lowe@brighthealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — multi-region pricing question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — the throughput numbers looked promising. Before we get legal/ procurement involved I need a clearer picture of how Redwood would price a Dedicated footprint for BrightHealth across two regions (US East, EU West). Specific asks from my side: 

- Can you give an example pricing breakdown for separate reserved pools per region vs a single primary pool with cross-region failover?
- What kinds of discounts are available on committed GPU-months and what are typical breakpoints (6/12/24 months)?
- Do you offer throughput guarantees (tokens/sec or rps) per pool, and what SLA credit triggers look like for Dedicated?
- Any additional cost for replication/DR or is that handled via routing and spare capacity?

We have to balance latency for our EU customers with cost controls — curious about the tradeoffs.

Appreciate any concrete numbers or a simple model we can take to procurement.

Best,
Adam
Adam Lowe
Director of Platform Engineering
BrightHealth Systems
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Adam Lowe <adam.lowe@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — multi-region pricing question

Hi Adam — thanks for the clear list. I looped in Marissa (SE) who can speak to sizing/throughput, and I can outline pricing and discount levers. High level summary up front: separate regional pools give predictable latency and simple isolation but increase committed spend; cross-region failover reduces committed footprint but requires warm/standby capacity and has slightly higher failover latencies.

I've attached a short pricing matrix that models three scenarios (regional independent pools, primary + standby, and single global pool with cross-region routing). See pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx.

Quick bullets: 
- Discount structure: 10% off list for 12-month committed GPU-months, 18% for 24 months, and up to ~25% for large enterprise commits (multi-region combined spends > $1.2M/year) — negotiable based on term and committed GPU count.
- Breakpoints: Typical breakpoints we model are 8 GPUs, 32 GPUs, 128 GPUs per region (these map to different packing/efficiency tiers).
- Throughput guarantees: We can offer per-pool throughput SLOs (e.g., 99.5% of requests under X ms / Y tokens/sec) with crediting tied to sustained shortfalls. Exact numbers depend on model family and sequence length — Marissa will propose per-model profiles.
- Replication/DR: Options: active-active (separate pools, traffic split), active-passive (primary + warm standby), or cross-region warm routing. Active-active is simplest for DR but doubles committed capacity if you fully mirror. Active-passive reduces cost but needs RPO/RTO expectations set.

Next steps: Marissa — can you add a short note on sizing assumptions and an estimate of the throughput we can guarantee for the Llama-3-70B variant at 2k context for both US/EU footprints? Adam — happy to set a 30-min pricing walk-through with procurement once we have the sizing numbers.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Aug 3, 2026 at 9:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference> wrote:
> I've attached a short pricing matrix...

Adam — quick sizing note from SE side. Assumptions: Llama-3-70B quantized to 8-bit server-optimized profile; target p95 token latency under 120ms for 512-token responses; typical user payload ~= 200 tokens per request. 

Estimated capacity guidance (approx):
- Small pool (8 x A40-equivalent GPUs): ~40 concurrent streams, ~25k tokens/sec aggregate, suitable for pilot/low-traffic EU/region.
- Mid pool (32 GPUs): ~160 concurrent streams, ~100k tokens/sec aggregate, typical for production verticals (customer-facing features).
- Large pool (128 GPUs): ~640 concurrent streams, ~400k tokens/sec aggregate for high-throughput use.

Throughput guarantees: we can commit to per-pool throughput SLOs expressed as aggregate tokens/sec and a percent of requests under latency targets (e.g., 99% of requests under 150ms at target load). SLA credits are typically a percentage of monthly committed fees for sustained violations (>10 mins).

Replication/DR tradeoffs: 
- If you require sub-60s failover and <1% request loss, we recommend active-passive with warm-standby at ~20-30% of primary capacity in the standby region plus cross-region prefix cache warming. 
- If you need near-zero failover impact, active-active with mirrored pools in each region is the recommendation — cost = roughly 2x committed capacity but gives the best latency/availability.

I'll attach a simple SLO template and an example SOW line item to the follow-up. Dev — can you add a short note about cross-region egress/costs and any networking prerequisites?

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of follow ups from procurement: 

- If we commit to 12 months for combined US+EU (say 32 GPUs US + 16 GPUs EU), is the discount applied on combined spend or per-region? Is there a single invoice or per-region billing?
- For the active-passive warm standby approach: you mentioned standby ~20-30% of primary. Does that standby need to be a committed reserve to get the discounted price, or can it be on-demand (we'd prefer reserved for predictability but want to avoid over-commitment).
- Can you confirm whether replication (model sync and KV cache seeding) is included as part of the Dedicated package or billed as an add-on professional services item?

Procurement also asked about an example pricing line for the model runtime (per-hour/GPU) and an indicative monthly committed invoice so they can run an internal TCO comparison against their current provider.

If you can send a short illustrative invoice (line items + totals) we can get legal/procurement moving.

—Adam
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — multi-region pricing question

Adam / Procurement — attaching an illustrative invoice and an SOW draft. High level answers: 

- Discounts: We apply the negotiated discount against your consolidated committed spend (so combined US+EU commits stack toward breakpoints). We can invoice per-region or consolidated monthly based on your preference — both supported.
- Standby: Warm-standby can be handled in two ways: as a committed reserved pool at the discounted committed rate (recommended for predictability and lower unit cost) or as on-demand burst capacity. If you prefer committed standby only for critical capacity, we can model hybrid (e.g., 80% reserved primary, 20% on-demand standby).
- Replication/model sync: Basic model deployment and KV cache seeding during rollouts are included in the Dedicated onboarding package (first rollout). Ongoing replication for active-active mirrored deployments is counted as sustained capacity (i.e., mirrored resources). If you want continuous cross-region DB/asset sync plus white-glove ops, that is offered as a professional-services add-on — we'll call this out in the SOW.

Attached: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx, sow-dedicated-multi-region.pdf. Also HubSpot link to deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890.

Proposed next step: 30-minute procurement call Thursday to walk through the illustrative invoice and we can put a preliminary term sheet together. I can send a DocuSign-ready term sheet once we agree the committed GPU counts and term (I included a sample DocuSign link for reference).

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
